title: Thai Green Curry
subtitle: Chicken and vegetables in a fragrant coconut green curry sauce
excerpt: Thai green curry (kaeng khiao wan) is one of the most aromatic curries in Thai cuisine: chicken and vegetables simmered in a rich coconut milk broth made with green curry paste, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. It is less fiery than red curry, with a fresher, herbaceous flavour from the green chillies and Thai basil.
sourceNotes: Kaeng khiao wan (literally sweet green curry) is one of the three main Thai curry styles alongside red and yellow. The green colour comes from fresh green chillies and green herbs in the paste. Commercially made green curry paste is an acceptable shortcut and produces excellent results. The dish is native to Central Thailand and became widely exported from the 1980s onwards.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the vegetables; add fresh when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales well. Make a large batch of sauce; portion and freeze.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

content.text: Fry the curry paste in the thick top of the coconut milk (the coconut cream) rather than in oil. This blooms the paste in fat and creates a more aromatic base than adding it to water. Do not add the remaining coconut milk until the paste has fried for 2 to 3 minutes and the oil has separated.

items.prepNote: do not shake — scoop off the thick cream from the top

content.text: Scoop the thick coconut cream from the top of the tin into a wide saucepan. Heat over medium heat. Add the green curry paste and fry, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until very fragrant and the oil starts to separate.
Add the chicken pieces. Coat in the paste and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the outside turns white.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and 100 ml of water. Add the kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the courgette and red pepper. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are just tender.
Taste and adjust with more fish sauce or sugar. Stir in the Thai basil. Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

items.symptom: Curry is watery and lacks flavour
items.cause: Paste was not fried long enough, or too much liquid was added
items.fix: Fry the paste aggressively in the coconut cream first. If the curry is thin, simmer uncovered for 5 to 10 minutes to reduce.
